input:
A shell-and-tube heat exchanger in a refinery preheat train heats crude oil by means of a hot process stream. The duty of the exchanger is 1726 kW. The hot stream enters at 180 °C and leaves at 130 °C, while the crude oil enters at 30 °C and leaves at 50 °C. The log-mean temperature difference for the exchanger works out at 114.3 K, and the installed area is 49.6 m2, which together give an overall heat transfer coefficient of 304 W m-2 K-1.

This coefficient is the value the installed area and the log-mean temperature difference return when combined with the stated duty: at a duty of 1726 kW, with an area of 49.6 m2 and a driving force of 114.3 K, the overall coefficient is 304 W m-2 K-1. The two streams undergo quite different changes in temperature, amounting to 50 K on the hot side, from 180 °C down to 130 °C, and 20 K on the cold side, from 30 °C up to 50 °C, and the log-mean difference of 114.3 K represents the driving force against which the area has been sized. The reported performance amounts to a single operating point: one duty, one pair of inlet and outlet temperatures for each stream, and one installed area.

Fouling was assessed on the basis of a single 90-day run, and no cleaning cycle has yet been completed. The coefficient of 304 W m-2 K-1 therefore rests upon a single 90-day fouling history, and neither performance following cleaning nor fouling behaviour over a longer period is covered by the figures reported here.

The hot stream enters at 180 °C and leaves at 130 °C; the crude oil enters at 30 °C and leaves at 50 °C. The log-mean temperature difference is 114.3 K and the installed area is 49.6 m2, giving an overall coefficient of 304 W m-2 K-1.

The coefficient is the value the installed area and the log-mean difference return at the stated duty: at 1726 kW, an area of 49.6 m2 and a driving force of 114.3 K give an overall coefficient of 304 W m-2 K-1. The reported performance is a single operating point: one duty, one pair of inlet and outlet temperatures for each stream, and one area. The two streams change temperature by different amounts: 50 K on the hot side, from 180 °C to 130 °C, and 20 K on the cold side, from 30 °C to 50 °C, and the log-mean difference of 114.3 K is the driving force the area is sized against.

Fouling was assessed from a single 90-day run, and no cleaning cycle has been completed. The coefficient of 304 W m-2 K-1 therefore rests on one 90-day fouling history: performance after cleaning, and fouling over a longer run, are not covered by the reported figures.
